title: Rigveda 10.161: Against emaciation
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (1711 CE (colophon: Saṃvat 1768)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 10.161: Against emaciation: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of a 1711 Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 10.161 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to against emaciation. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 10, the last and latest book. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 (University of Pennsylvania), a paper manuscript of the eighth aṣṭaka (RV 10.46-10.191) of the Ṛgveda Saṃhitā in Devanāgarī, 158 leaves, 6 lines to the page, with the accents marked in red; the scribe's colophon on fol. 158 gives Saṃvat 1768 (1711 CE); this hymn stands on fol. 140r-140v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Like most Rigveda manuscripts, Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 writes a repeated refrain in short form after its first occurrence (for example kasmai° for kasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema); the Sanskrit shown is the full text of Aufrecht's edition.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).

translation.original_ref: RV 10.161.1-2 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 19); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 140r
translation.original_text:
1mu̱ñcāmi̍ tvā ha̱viṣā̱ jīva̍nāya̱ kam a̍jñātaya̱kṣmād u̱ta rā̍jaya̱kṣmāt | grāhi̍r ja̱grāha̱ yadi̍ vai̱tad e̍na̱ṁ tasyā̍ indrāgnī̱ pra mu̍muktam enam ||
2yadi̍ kṣi̱tāyu̱r yadi̍ vā̱ pare̍to̱ yadi̍ mṛ̱tyor a̍nti̱kaṁ nī̍ta e̱va | tam ā ha̍rāmi̱ nirṛ̍ter u̱pasthā̱d aspā̍rṣam enaṁ śa̱taśā̍radāya ||
translation.text:
1FOR life I set thee free by this oblation from the unknown decline and from Consumption; Or, if the grasping demon have possessed him, free him from her, O Indra, thou and Agni.
2Be his days ended, be he now departed, be he brought very near to death already, Out of Destruction's lap again I bring him, save him for life to last a hundred autumns.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 140r (OPenn image 139, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.160.3 ‹-praśastam ic cārum asmai›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 140v, begins in RV 10.161.3 ‹sahasrākṣeṇa śataśāradena śatāyuṣā haviṣāhārṣam›. Verses 10.161.1-2 end on this page.

translation.original_ref: RV 10.161.3-5 (aṣṭaka 8, adhyāya 8, varga 19); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48 fol. 140v
translation.original_text:
3sa̱ha̱srā̱kṣeṇa̍ śa̱taśā̍radena śa̱tāyu̍ṣā ha̱viṣāhā̍rṣam enam | śa̱taṁ yathe̱maṁ śa̱rado̱ nayā̱tīndro̱ viśva̍sya duri̱tasya̍ pā̱ram ||
4śa̱taṁ jī̍va śa̱rado̱ vardha̍mānaḥ śa̱taṁ he̍ma̱ntāñ cha̱tam u̍ vasa̱ntān | śa̱tam i̍ndrā̱gnī sa̍vi̱tā bṛha̱spati̍ḥ śa̱tāyu̍ṣā ha̱viṣe̱mam puna̍r duḥ ||
5āhā̍rṣa̱ṁ tvāvi̍daṁ tvā̱ puna̱r āgā̍ḥ punarnava | sarvā̍ṅga̱ sarva̍ṁ te̱ cakṣu̱ḥ sarva̱m āyu̍ś ca te 'vidam ||
translation.text:
3With hundred-eyed oblation, hundred-autumned, bringing a hundred lives, have I restored him, That Indra for a hundred years may lead him safe to the farther shore of all misfortune.
4Live, waxing in thy strength, a hundred autumns, live through a hundred springs, a hundred winters. Through hundred-lived oblation Indra, Agni, Br̥ihaspati, Savitar yield him for a hundred!
5So have I found and rescued thee thou hast returned with youth renewed. Whole in thy members! I have found thy sight and all thy life for thee.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 48, fol. 140v (OPenn image 140, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 10.161.3 ‹sahasrākṣeṇa śataśāradena śatāyuṣā haviṣāhārṣam›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 141r, begins in RV 10.162.1 ‹durṇāmā yonim āśaye›. Verses 10.161.3-5 end on this page.
